Rendered knowledge base

A client rendered application initially exposes only an empty mount point. After its application state arrives, the page contains the complete guide that readers need. The renderer must hand this settled document to the same extractor and independent verifier used for static pages. That keeps browser rendering an adopted transport engine rather than a second honesty system with weaker rules.

Client state

The visible document includes navigation context, explanatory prose, and stable section labels. Loading is considered successful only after the page state has produced meaningful content. A short shell is not promoted to success, even when its network response was two hundred. The browser tier preserves the final URL and response status so provenance remains factual and reviewable.

Verified output

Extraction happens after rendering, then the verifier compares the rendered DOM with the extracted Markdown. Heading presence, visible word coverage, declared length, block-page checks, and pagination remain independent facts. Two positive content signals are required before the result can be called complete. If those facts disagree, OmniRead reports an incomplete or unknown result instead of manufacturing certainty.
